features.name: title_has_emotional_or_personal_identifier
features.definition: Does the title contain an explicit emotional expression or personal identifier (e.g., first-person self-reference or stated feelings)?
features.spec: Read only the title. Return 1 if the title contains an explicit emotional term/expression (e.g., 'I hate', 'I feel', 'angry', 'love', 'scared') or an explicit personal identifier of the poster (e.g., first-person self-reference such as I/my/me, or self-described identity/experience such as 'as a woman', 'I'm a veteran'). Return 0 otherwise. Ignore the 'CMV:' prefix. Quoted wording counts only if the poster adopts it as their own. Missing/empty title gives null. Exclude any view-change/delta announcements (unlikely in titles).

h0: title_has_emotional_or_personal_identifier has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: Posts with title_has_emotional_or_personal_identifier=1 have a lower probability of OP view change than those with 0.
note: Operational assumption: "emotional or personal identifiers" is treated as a single binary presence of either explicit emotion wording or first-person/self-identity markers in the title; the two are not separated. OLS on binary delta (linear probability model). Association only. Titles are current text and could theoretically contain edits.
